transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... I guess I'm just tired all the time. Um, by midmorning at work—I'm a claims adjuster—after just reviewing some files or, you know, walking a junior adjuster through a claim... it just feels like my body and my brain are already running on empty. So... that's why I'm here.
Have you noticed that you're not enjoying things as much as you used to, or that you don't really feel like doing things you once enjoyed?

I guess... yeah. It just feels like... I don't know, like there's a gray film over things most days. Even when my husband is being kind, or... if we're cooking with the family. I just sort of go through the motions. I don't really feel the enjoyment I used to.
Have you noticed a decrease in your energy levels or an increase in fatigue, even after getting enough rest?

Yeah... um, like I mentioned earlier, I'm just tired all the time. It doesn't really seem to matter if I sleep. By midmorning at work, after just looking over a few files, my body and my brain are just... running on empty.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately?
Um... no, not really. I haven't noticed anything like that. I guess I eat about the same as usual.
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty or like you’re not worth much lately?
Um... no. I don't think so. I haven't really noticed feeling like that.
Have you noticed that you've been moving more slowly than usual, or maybe fidgeting more without meaning to?
No... I don't think I've been doing either of those things. Just... working at my normal pace, I guess.
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these feelings lasted for more than two weeks?

It's... it's been a lot longer than two weeks. Um... I guess it's been about three years, maybe a little more. Three years and a few months. Ever since they... um, moved me into a different role at work, overseeing the new systems and mentoring the other adjusters. It's just been since then.
Have you had days where you felt down or hopeless almost every day, and if so, how often does this occur and how long does it last?

Yeah... like I said, it's been a few years now. And I guess it's most days. It just... I don't know, it feels like there's a gray film over everything. Um... even when my husband is being kind, or if we're cooking with the family... I just sort of go through the motions. I don't really feel the enjoyment I used to.
Have you had trouble sleeping, or have you found yourself sleeping much more than usual lately?
No... not really. I sleep about the same as I always do, I guess. It hasn't really changed.
Have you ever felt like life isn't worth living, or had thoughts about hurting yourself?
No. No, I haven't. I just... I just feel down, that's all.
Have you noticed any trouble with your ability to think clearly, concentrate, or make decisions lately?
No... not really. I haven't noticed any problems with that. I can still do my work and everything fine.

Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually high, extremely energetic, or irritable for several days at a time, or had times where you felt both depressed and overly energized or restless in the same day or week?
No... I haven't. Nothing like that. Just... just the way I've been feeling.
Have you ever had a period of time before this where you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?
No, I... I don't think so. It's just been this sort of low feeling, like I said. Nothing... nothing that intense or specific.
Before this current period of feeling down, have you ever had any other times in your life when you felt persistently sad or lost interest in things for a couple of weeks or more?
No... I think you just asked me that. But no, I haven't. It's just been this... same low feeling for a long time now. I don't remember any specific times before this.
Can you recall if you ever had any other periods in your life before this current one where you felt down or uninterested in things for several weeks or more?
I... didn't we just go over this? No. I haven't. It's just been this same feeling.
Can you recall if there were any significant stressors or difficult life events around the time you were moved into the new role at work and started feeling this way?
No... not really. Nothing stands out. It was just the new role. I don't think anything else was going on.
Can you recall if there were any times in your life when you felt completely back to normal between the start of this low feeling and now?
No... not really. I don't think so. It's just... it's just been the same for a long time. I haven't really felt normal.
Have you ever had a time when you felt so good or so irritable that people around you noticed a change in your mood or behavior, even if it only lasted a few days?
No. I... I don't think so. I haven't had anything like that. Just... just what I've been telling you.
Have you ever had a time when you felt unusually excited, overly confident, or needed less sleep but still had plenty of energy, even if it only lasted a few days?
No... I haven't. I don't really get excited like that. And I've always needed my sleep... so, no. Nothing like that.

inference_history.note: The patient endorsed persistent fatigue and anhedonia, which are key features of depressive disorders. This makes major depressive disorder (F32, F33) and persistent depressive disorder (F34.1) more likely. Other disorders such as insomnia (G47) and unspecified nonorganic sleep disorders (G47.8, G47.9) are less likely at this point given the absence of prominent sleep complaints. Neurotic disorder (F48.0), panic disorder (F48.1), and other specified/unspecified disorders (F48.8, F48.9) are also less likely given the current presentation.

The duration of symptoms (approximately three years) rules out episodic disorders (F32.x) and supports the consideration of recurrent or persistent depressive disorders. F34.1 (Dysthymia) is included due to the chronic nature of symptoms, while F33.x codes remain due to possible recurrent major depressive episodes. F32.0-9 and F33.0 are excluded due to duration and presentation.

The chronic nature of the symptoms (approximately 3 years) and the absence of manic or hypomanic symptoms, psychotic features, and significant functional impairment rules out F34.1 (Persistent Depressive Disorder) as the primary diagnosis. However, the possibility of a recurrent major depressive disorder (F33.1, F33.2, F33.3) or unspecified recurrent depression (F33.9) remains appropriate given the persistent depressive symptoms nearly every day, lack of change in sleep/appetite/psychomotor activity, and preserved cognitive function.
